assets.title: Who keeps the Slack bot running after you build it
assets.content:
Subject: Who keeps the Slack bot running after you build it
Preview text: Nobody, if you configure one instead. orqAgent is hosted, installs by OAuth, and logs every answer.

orqAgent: configure the handbook bot, don't build it

Hi there,

The question is not whether you can build a Slack answer-bot over the handbook. It is who owns it in March, when whoever built it has moved on.

Meanwhile the same policy questions keep coming back in Slack, and the answers sit in documentation people search by guessing at page titles.

A low-code stack gets a bot answering fast. By the account of the people who build them, it is not made for reliable production use — and it leaves you running a vector store so a bot can answer from a PDF.

orqAgent is available today — a hosted place to configure one agent over your own handbook documents. Slack is an OAuth install, so the bot replies to mentions and channel messages.

You upload the PDFs, docs or plain text. The agent retrieves the most relevant context for every query automatically — no vector DB to manage.

P95 latency, token usage per model and daily spend trends are tracked automatically, without extra config. What it answered and what it cost is a page you open, not a dashboard someone has to build.

Start for free — one agent, one set of policy documents, one Slack channel, and the questions your team asks most.

Create your first agent →

- the orqAgent team

P.S. Setup runs from the console in under two minutes, and no credit card is required to start.

emails.single_idea: orqAgent is available now: point an agent at your own handbook documents, connect it to Slack, and the repeat policy questions get answered in the channel — without you standing up or maintaining the retrieval layer underneath it.

reader_verdicts.what_it_sells: A no-code platform (orqAgent) for building an AI agent that connects to your handbook/Notion docs and installs into Slack to answer employee questions automatically, without you having to build or maintain the retrieval/hosting infrastructure yourself.
reader_verdicts.relevance_feedback: Email-only: it assumes the reader has already weighed building this exact bot and is deterred by owning 'Slack events, a vector store, a model API' indefinitely — that specific dread is not confirmed by the profile, only that this person 'has been asked to build or is considering building' one. Profile-supported: the profile explicitly names Handbook/Docs/Issue Trackers as the target sources and Slack as the channel where repeat questions land, which the email's core scenario matches closely for Handbook and Notion docs. Gap: the profile also names Issue Trackers as a required source, and the email never mentions Issue Trackers at all, so the premise is only partially covered for someone whose actual ask includes that.
assumed_experiences: That the reader has already considered or been asked to build a Slack bot over the handbook and dreads owning the infrastructure (email-only, consistent with but not confirmed by profile's 'considering building')
That the reader's docs live in Notion or are uploadable files (profile-supported)
That the reader has personally fielded repeat policy questions by hand (profile-supported — profile states people ping this person directly)
That 'no vector DB to manage' and 'serverless' fully resolve the reliability/scale concerns of a production internal tool (email-only assertion, unverified)
reader_verdicts.problem_now: Documented as a current, ongoing pain in the supplied context (repeated policy questions, answers buried in hard-to-navigate docs) — not a hypothetical or scheduled event, so it reads as relevant to today, not just someday.
reader_verdicts.stopped_at: So people search by guessing document titles, and when that fails they ping a person.
reader_verdicts.biggest_doubt: This is an unknown vendor asking to ingest internal handbook/policy documents, and the email says nothing about where that data lives, who can see it, or any compliance posture — for someone standing this up for a whole company, that's the first question, and it isn't addressed. Also unclear how a 'no-code' single-agent, single-document-set demo scales to Handbook + Docs + Issue Trackers together, or what it costs past the free first agent.
reader_verdicts.to_click_it_would_have_to: told me where the uploaded/synced documents are stored and who has access to them, or said whether it can also pull from an issue tracker (Jira/GitHub) rather than just Notion/files — that's the one part of my actual ask this doesn't address.
fixes:
Now available

Nobody wants to own another internal bot — this reads as disconnected header fragments before the greeting, unclear if it's a subhead, a section title, or stray preview text.
with no vector DB to manage — states the absence of a component without saying what actually happens to the data or who can see it, which is exactly the question a company-docs use case raises.

P.S. If you have already been asked to stand one up, this is the short version of that task. — vague callback that assumes context about a 'task' the email never actually described in full elsewhere, reads as filler.
